Definition: from G1097; well-known:--acquaintance, (which may be) known, notable.
BiblicalUsage: gnōstós means acquaintance, (which may be) known, notable. In Luke 2:44, the text says "and they sought him among [their] kinsfolk and acquaintance." In John 18:15, the text says "that disciple was known unto the high priest."
TheologicalSignificance: Reading gnōstós this way, I believe the gospel was never meant to stay where it started — it goes out, because God sends it out. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
RelatedEvents: The Birth of Jesus; The Choice of Matthias; The Boy Jesus in the Temple
